enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . .KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 458 PM MDT Thu Oct 15 2026

 - A strong backdoor cold front moves in this evening, bringing 
   gusty winds and well below normal temperatures into the 
   weekend. 

 - High Wind Warning is in effect for far west Texas and portions
   of southern New Mexico for Thursday night into Friday. Wind 
   gusts up to 60 mph are possible along mountain west slopes. 

 - Scattered rain showers starting Monday and continuing through
   next Thursday as temperatures rebound.

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 927 AM MDT Thu Oct 15 2026

The north wind doth blow this early afternoon as an upper-level 
low moves across the Rockies. But once the sun nears the horizon, 
the winds will shift east and increase drastically, for a backdoor
cold front of formidable strength will reach our area early this
evening. The backdoor cold front stems from a combination of the 
upper-level low splitting into two this afternoon, with the second
circulation moving southwest towards Arizona, and a strong surface
high in the northern Rockies filling the void the upper-level low
has left, bringing a surge of cooler air into our region tonight.
3
The cold front boundary shall reach the El Paso/Las Cruces metro 
areas this evening. With this cold front is a tight pressure
gradient and a low level jet that will bring sustained east-
northeast winds of 25 to 35 mph for most of the region. Wind gusts
exceeding 60 mph are expected for Otero, Hudspeth, and El Paso
Counties tonight and into tomorrow, particularly along the west
slopes of the mountains. High Wind Warnings are in effect for 
these counties, as well as southern Hidalgo and Grant Counties, 
through tomorrow night. The rest of the county warning area is 
under a Wind Advisory, with gusts up to 50 mph, through tomorrow 
night. Blowing dust is likely with these strong winds in El Paso 
and Hudspeth Counties in Texas, and southern Dona Ana and Luna 
Counties in New Mexico, beginning late this evening. The playas 
in Hidalgo County is also expected to see blowing dust on Friday.

Temperatures for the region will plunge to at least 20 degrees
below normal tonight thanks to the cold air advection associated 
with the cold front. Friday and Saturday will be a struggle for 
daytime high temperatures to reach the lower 60s in the lowlands.
Freezing temperatures are expected for the mountains both on
Friday and Saturday morning. It is likely we shall not have snow 
or even rain in the mountains, for a surge in moisture in previous
model runs has shifted south. Rain is not expected to be a factor
for our region this weekend.

Once the winds die down Sunday, temperatures will begin their
steady climb back to seasonal normals. The cutoff low will be in
the Baja by this point and weakened enough to be folded into a
passing ridge, bringing subtropical moisture into the region as
early as Sunday afternoon. The Animas Mountains in the New Mexico
bootheel will see a slight chance of showers Sunday afternoon, and
a greater chance of rain showers across the region is expected to
start Monday afternoon. A new Pacific trough will help facilitate
shower chances across the region early next week, though how much
rain the region will get through next Thursday remains to be seen.

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 458 PM MDT Thu Oct 15 2026

Backdoor cold front arrives early in period, increasing winds
around 3z. Gusts up to 40kts overnight from NE, excluding KLRU
which looks to be in a pocket of lighter winds. Dust models are
picking up on BLDU for KELP tonight, most likely from 3-6z. Low
chance of VIS dropping to 1SM at KELP, but confidence is low. BLDU
chances are low at best for the other terminals tonight. LLWS can
be seen also overnight. Winds lighten a bit during the day and 
shift more E. Mainly SKC throughout.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 927 AM MDT Thu Oct 15 2026

Low end breezy winds from the north will define this early
afternoon. Min RHs in the lowlands are in the mid-to-upper teens
and in the upper-20s-to-low-30's across the mountains. A drastic
change is afoot this evening as a backdoor cold front arrives from
the northeast, shifting winds eastward and dropping temperatures
to at least 20 degrees below average. Sustained wind speeds
tonight and into tomorrow will range from 25-35 mph are wide, with
wind gusts exceeding 60 mph along the west slopes of the
mountains. Min RHs Friday and Saturday will continue to be in the
mid-to-upper teens in the lowlands, and fall to the 20s in the
mountains. Temperatures will gradually warm up and winds will die
down on Sunday, with a chance for rain early next week.
